 Montgomery County District Court
 Cause No. 2025-CV-0005
 Samuel Carter, Plaintiff, v. Harbor Point Mutual Auto Insurance, Defendant
 Plaintiff's Original Petition
Filed:
September 26, 2025
Plaintiff's counsel:
Sergio Acosta, Gardner & Morris Law Group
PARTIES
Plaintiff Samuel Carter is an individual who resides in Texas and was the driver of a passenger vehicle involved in the collision
described below. Defendant is the automobile liability insurer that issued the policy under which the at-fault driver was insured at
the time of the collision. Defendant may be served through its registered agent for service of process in the State of Texas.
FACTS
On October 18, 2023, Plaintiff was lawfully operating his vehicle on a public roadway in Sugar Land, Texas, when anohter
vehicle, operated by a driver insured under Defendant's policy, entered the intersection and struck the side of Plaintiff's car. The
impact was severe enough to disable both vehicles. Plaintiff reported the collision promptly, provided a recorded statement, and
submitted the documentation Defendant requested. Defendant accepted coverage responsibility for the at-fault driver but has not
paid the reasonable value of Plaintiff's losses.
NEGLIGENCE
The at-fault driver owed a duty to exercise ordinary care in operating a motor vehicle, including yielding the right of way and
keeping a proper lookout. That driver breached this duty, and the breach porximately caused the collision and Plaintiff's injuries.
Defendant, as liability insurer, is obligated under its policy to pay damages its insured becomes legally obligated to pay, and it
has failed to make a reasonable settlement offer after liability became reasonably clear, in violation of the Texas Insurance Code
and the duties of good faith and fair dealing.
DAMAGES
As a direct result of the collision, Plaintiff suffered serious and permanent injuries that have caused ongoing pain, limited
mobility, and lost earning capacity. Plaintiff has incurred substantial medical expenses and will require future medical care,
including further treatment and rehabilitation, for the remainder of his life. Plaintiff seeks recovery of past and future medical
expenses, lost wages, physical pain and mental anguish, physical impairment, and other damaegs allowed by Texas law, in an
amount of $75,600.00, together with prejudgment and postjudgment interest, court costs, and all other relief to which Plaintiff
may be entitled.
